newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Vnukovo airline to operate two new Tu-204s.
newsitem.headline: Russian Vnukovo airline to operate two new Tu-204s.

text.p: Russia's biggest domestic air carrier Vnukovo Airlines will start operating two new Tupolev-204 passenger and cargo jets this week, increasing its fleet to 56 aircraft, a senior company official said on Monday.

Sergei Komasko, the airline's chief sales manager, told Reuters that the company would also begin scheduled charters from Moscow to Tenerife in the Canary Islands and to Hurghada in Egypt later this month.
Komasko said the carrier planned to expand its domestic route network, introducing regular flights from Moscow to five destinations -- Magnitogorsk, Chelyabinsk, Bratsk, Novokuznetsk and Perm.
"Two of these routes will be opened by the end of the year," he added.
Komasko also said Vnukovo Airlines had increased passenger and cargo loads by 5-7 percent during the first nine months of this year compared with the same period of 1995. He gave no further details.

The company carried 812,000 passengers in the first half of this year, down from 860,000 in the same period last year. It also carried 6,990 tonnes of mail and freight during the first six months. In January-June 1995, it carried 7,463 tonnes.
In 1995, Vnukovo Airlines carried 1.9 million passengers and 15,300 tonnes of cargo and mail.
Komasko said the company planned to expand its cargo deliveries. "Recently we set up a freight department which linked with leading Russian and Western forwarders," he said.

Moscow-based Vnukovo Airlines was set up in 1993 after former Soviet state monopoly Aeroflot was split. The company operates regular flights to 28 domestic destinations and runs 16 scheduled international charter routes.
